title: A big festival day in Thatcham
summary: Saturday saw a number of events attracting local people as as part of Thatcham Town Council's annual festival where the best of Thatcham was on show. Our team was out and about reporting from the events.
imageAlt: A lady stood by a table packed with knitted animal toys, which she is offering for sale
caption: Celia Camplin displays her hand knitted toys for sale

content.text:
Saturday was a big day in Thatcham as events ran across the town by organisations showcasing the best of what they do.

St Mary's Church was a popular venue where over a hundred people came to buy from the many stalls at the craft fair, listen to the music, and enjoy a cup of tea and a cake. Mrs. Celia Camplin, (pictured above), was one of the many stallholders offering her knitted toy products to the visitors who came along.

the Thatcham Historical Society was also present at the church, where members were displaying pictures and educating visitors about the history of Thatcham from the evidence of the very earliest prehistoric life forms, the earliest human settlements through to the modern town that Thatcham is today.

content.imageAlt: The Thatcham Historical Society stand at St Mary's Church during the Thatcham Festival
content.caption: Visitors to the Thatcham Historical Society learn about the interesting history of Thatcham

content.text: Elsewhere in the town, an event was held, looking at the historical and modern uses of different plants. The 'Herbal Histories' event in the Jubilee Sensory Garden next to the Thatcham Town Council offices gave visitors the opportunity to join a walk and talk around the Sensory Garden and to learn how to make an herbal balm to take home.

content.imageAlt: A picture of a raised box containing various plants at the Jubilee Sensory Garden
content.caption: Jubilee Sensory Garden

content.text:
The Broadway was busy after being taken over by local clubs and societies, showcasing what they do and hoping to recruit some new members. A popular attraction was the gazebo hosted by Newbury Astronomical Society (NAS). The members shared pictures and displayed various telescopes for visitors to try looking through.

The star attraction on the NAS display was a telescope fitted with a solar filter allowing people to safely observe the sun. Steve Harris from the NAS said this was particularly useful during the practical social eclipse on 12th August. NAS welcomes new members and is currently running evening meetings for beginners.

content.imageAlt: A man looking into a telescope
content.caption: Steve Harris from Newbury Astronomical Society observing the sun

content.text: The Thatcham branch of University of the Third Age (u3a) had its gazebo in the Broadway. The u3a welcomes retired people who want to meet other like minded people who enjoy attending talks, activities and learning new skills. Thatcham u3a has regular coffee mornings and meetings around Thatcham.

content.imageAlt: A gazebo in high street manned by members of u3a
content.caption: The u3a gazebo with members explaining u3a to visitors

content.text:
Newbury and District Hackspace held a retro and computer gaming exhibition at its home next to The Moors Playing Fields in Thatcham. The event showed earlier home computers and video games from the 1970s onwards and allowed visitors to have a go. Systems on display included working examples of the Commodore PET and the BBC Computer and offered excitement for younger visitors and nostalgia for those who were kids in the 1970s.

The Hackspace members create, craft, mend, re-purpose, share, teach and learn in a community workshop with modern professional equipment. Members can come along and learn about Laser cutting, 3D printing, metal working, electronics, CAD, CAM software and more.

content.imageAlt: A picture of old computer systems dating back to the 1970s on show at an exhibition
content.caption: 1970s tech on display at the Newbury and District Hackspace Exhibition
